This turns that into a rhythm, a set of repeatable plays, and the specific mechanics for each. 8 9 --- 10 11 ## 1. The mandate, consolidated 12 13 What the sessions actually assigned you: 14 15 | # | Responsibility | From | 16 |---|---|---| 17 | 1 | Own dependency discovery during refinement | M1 — the strongest expectation raised | 18 | 2 | Protect Salesforce / PWA Kit reuse; challenge "let's build this" | M1 | 19 | 3 | Own component governance — prevent duplicate Buttons, Links, utilities | M1 | 20 | 4 | Strengthen FE PR review criteria | M1 | 21 | 5 | Improve estimation accuracy — surface hidden work before planning | M1 (Jasmijn, repeatedly) | 22 | 6 | Embed accessibility in component stories, not as follow-up | M1 + M2 | 23 | 7 | Follow up design-system gaps with Kiera / design owners | M1 | 24 | 8 | Define the atoms governance model + a refinement checklist | M1 (strategic) | 25 | 9 | Component completeness — all variants designed upfront | M2 | 26 | 10 | Define a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components | M2 | 27 | 11 | Ensure components gracefully handle optional fields | M2 | 28 | 12 | Document accessibility expectations component-by-component | M2 | 29 | 13 | Own page-level validation — visual, responsive, integration, design parity | M2 | 30 | 14 | Push back where requirements are unclear before sizing | M2 | 31 | 15 | Support incremental assembly (build → drop in → verify) | M2 | 32 | 16 | Separate component-build effort from page-composition effort in estimates | M2 | 33 34 **The through-line, in Tim's words:** *"FED leadership needs to identify what already exists before the team commits to building something new."* 35 36 **The one to resist as stated.** #1 makes you a serial gate across both squads' refinement sessions. It won't scale and it will slip. Play 1 handles this by moving the lookup to where the story is drafted and keeping only the judgement calls for yourself. 37 38 --- 39 40 ## 2. Your operating rhythm 41 42 Sixteen responsibilities, four moments. Everything below hangs off this. 43 44 | When | Plays | Time | 45 |---|---|---| 46 | **Story drafting** (BA-initiated, async) | 1 — reuse & dependency check | Async, minutes per story | 47 | **Refinement** (per story) | 1, 3, 9, 14 — dependencies, variants, push-back | In the session | 48 | **Pre-sprint-planning** (weekly) | 2 — estimation validation | ~30 min | 49 | **PR review** (continuous) | 5 — the human-only checks | Per PR | 50 | **Design review** (weekly, with Kiera) | 6 — design-system gaps | Standing slot | 51 52 Two standing items that don't fit a cadence: the **renderer contract** (Play 4, once per Contentful component) and **page-level validation** (Play 7, once per page assembly). 53 54 --- 55 56 ## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check 57 58 *Covers responsibilities 1, 2, 3, 8* 59 60 ### The ladder (agreed in M1) 61 62 ``` 63 Salesforce / PWA Kit capability 64 ↓ (nothing fits) 65 Existing shared component in overrides/ 66 ↓ (nothing fits) 67 Existing pattern 68 ↓ (nothing fits) 69 New implementation ← justify this out loud 70 ``` 71 72 ### Where to actually look 73 74 | Question | Source | 75 |---|---| 76 | Does a Base, Override or Custom component already exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` — columns: **Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers**. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change | 77 | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | 78 | What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` | 79 | Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` | 80 | What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | 81 82 The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below). 83 84 ### Worked examples, already verified 85 86 | Ask | What already exists | 87 |---|---| 88 | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test | 89 | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant | 90 | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | 91 | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | 92 93 Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration. 94 95 ### The hidden cost to name every time 96 97 If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work: 98 99 1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` 100 2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports 101 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 102 4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker 103 5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base** 104 6. Then build; remove markers 105 106 It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly. 107 108 ### Making this scale (the fix for #1) 109 110 Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093: 111 112 > *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."* 113 114 That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement: 115 116 - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** 117 - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** 118 119 ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) 120 121 The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: 122 123 - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. 124 - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. 125 - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. 126 127 Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. 128 129 --- 130 131 ## Play 2 — Estimation validation 132 133 *Covers responsibilities 5, 16* 134 135 Run this before sprint planning, not in it. 136 137 ### The re-baseline to communicate once 138 139 M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence: 140 141 - **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper. 142 - **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.** 143 144 Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch. 145 146 If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly. 147 148 ### Split the two kinds of effort (#16) 149 150 | Component build | Page composition | 151 |---|---| 152 | Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration | 153 | Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing | 154 | Storybook + tests | Visual validation | 155 | Sized as build work | Sized as validation work | 156 157 Don't let them be estimated with the same scale. 158 159 ### Challenge list 160 161 For each story before it's sized: 162 163 - [ ] `Origin = Base`? → Copy-first cost is in, or split out 164 - [ ] All variants captured, or only the ones on the first page? 165 - [ ] Accessibility written as AC, or assumed? 166 - [ ] Storybook story accounted for? 167 - [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column) 168 - [ ] Does it depend on anything in Play 8's open list? 169 - [ ] Composition variant hiding as a configuration variant? (Play 3) 170 171 --- 172 173 ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review 174 175 *Covers responsibilities 9, 11* 176 177 M2's rule: a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. 178 179 ### The distinction to hold 180 181 | Kind | Examples | How it's built | 182 |---|---|---| 183 | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | 184 | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | 185 186 This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. 187 188 Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. 189 190 ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference 191 192 The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. 193 194 ### Optional-field handling (#11) 195 196 M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. 197 198 --- 199 200 ## Play 4 — The renderer contract 201 202 *Covers responsibility 10* 203 204 M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. 205 206 **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* 207 208 **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. 209 210 | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | 211 |---|---|---|---|---|---| 212 | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | 213 | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | 214 | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | 215 | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | 216 | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | 217 218 **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. 219 220 **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. 221 222 **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Which pattern a given component uses is still unresolved (Play 8). 223 224 --- 225 226 ## Play 5 — PR review 227 228 *Covers responsibility 4* 229 230 The useful move here is knowing what the tooling already catches, so your attention goes where it's actually needed. 231 232 ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time on it 233 234 | Check | Enforced by | 235 |---|---| 236 | Missing `alt` on `` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | 237 | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | 238 | `onClick` on non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | 239 | Payment credentials logged | semgrep `payment-credential-logged` | 240 | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` | 241 | Type errors, lint, conventional commits | `tsc --noEmit`, lint, commit-msg hook | 242 | Registry freshness | pre-commit hook | 243 244 ### Not enforced — this is your list 245 246 | Gap | Why it matters | 247 |---|---| 248 | **Hardcoded hex / px values** in Chakra props and `.scss` | `css.md` states plainly it isn't mechanically enforced. Highest-frequency design-system violation | 249 | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | 250 | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | 251 | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | 252 | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | 253 254 Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. 255 256 ### Review questions, in order 257 258 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 259 2. Are all design values tokens? 260 3. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 261 4. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 262 5. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 263 6. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? 264 265 --- 266 267 ## Play 6 — Accessibility 268 269 *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* 270 271 M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. 272 273 ### The per-component AC set (#12) 274 275 Standing list to apply to every component story: 276 277 - Keyboard operability and reachability 278 - Focus order and visible focus states 279 - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) 280 - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls 281 - Behaviour when optional content is absent 282 283 **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate. 284 285 ### The one open item 286 287 M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter. 288 289 **Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision. The BA guide flags it as pending rather than settled. 290 291 --- 292 293 ## Play 7 — Page-level validation 294 295 *Covers responsibilities 13, 15* 296 297 M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout, design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX. 298 299 ### Where each part lands today 300 301 | Ask | Home | 302 |---|---| 303 | Assembled UX / integration | ✅ Playwright E2E — `@area` tags `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations` | 304 | Performance | ✅ `lighthouserc.js` | 305 | Responsive behaviour | ⚠️ Partial — Playwright runs desktop + mobile Chrome, but asserts behaviour, not appearance | 306 | **Spacing / design fidelity / design parity** | ❌ **No automated home.** `testing.md` explicitly excludes visual snapshots from the Vitest budget | 307 308 **Name this rather than absorbing it.** Design-parity validation is currently manual visual QA. Either it's accepted as manual and the time is resourced, or it's a visual-regression tooling decision (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) — a new dependency and budget, which needs approval before anything is installed. An unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here. 309 310 Operational note: only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in the change-scoping config. Each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group, or it silently falls back to the full suite. 311 312 ### Incremental assembly (#15) 313 314 Tim's build → drop-in → verify loop is well supported and costs nothing to adopt: 315 316 | Step | Support | 317 |---|---| 318 | Build in isolation | Storybook — mandatory story; `Contentful/` category explicitly allows mock CMS data | 319 | Make available to authors | `npm run generate:contentful` regenerates definitions; pre-commit keeps it in sync | 320 | Author drops it on a page | Studio Experiences — appears once annotated | 321 | Verify | `pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` routes exist | 322 323 **Caveat worth stating:** this loop only works for Studio Experiences components. Entry-driven ones are wired in code and aren't drag-and-droppable. Another reason the pattern question in Play 8 matters. 324 325 --- 326 327 ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing 328 329 *Covers responsibility 14* 330 331 These were explicitly left unresolved. Your job is to keep them from being sized on assumption. 332 333 | Open item | Position to hold | 334 |---|---| 335 | **Alt text** | Confirm with Tim before it lands in AC — Play 6 | 336 | **External links** | Already answered in draft AC (internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Adopt it, bake it into the Link component when built. Doesn't need another meeting | 337 | **Recommendations** | Not actually unknown — `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed, requirement-traced tickets (112, 118, 119, 313, 314, 642, 647, plus 301 under Cart). **SFCC-647 is already `Ready for Development`** and is the one that answers the data-source question. All are Priority `Low`, which is why they surfaced as unknowns. Raise 647; don't create tickets | 338 | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names in circulation for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (M2 + SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7, marked Done), and `shoppableImage` (which already exists in code and delivers exactly the manual curation Bianca described). Resolve to one name per capability before estimating | 339 | **Preview & publishing** | Documented: the preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only, never staging or prod; both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** Settle it now — "can we preview on prod?" is a likely later ask, and it needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale | 340 | **Contentful pattern per component** | Still unresolved after two sessions, and it decides story order, whether the incremental-assembly loop is available, and whether a component is buildable as specified. **Highest-value item to close** | 341 | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across 8 storefronts. Prerequisite to "design variants upfront" | 342 | **Composed-page ownership** | Tim's *"not product/category → Contentful"* rule is a good default but doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks, category landing pages, or promotional tiles in navigation. Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight | 343 344 **A process note worth acting on.** The Size Selector / Add To Bag split was argued and settled in a Jira comment thread two weeks before M1 re-derived it. Decisions made in refinement need somewhere findable to live, or they get re-litigated. Cheapest fix: when a decision lands, it goes on the story *and* into the relevant Confluence page — not just the thread. 345 346 --- 347 348 ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation 349 350 *Covers responsibility 7* 351 352 Standing agenda for the design review with Kiera. Two concrete items rather than a general "validate button states": 353 354 1. **Button** — 04.7 lists *"Style: Primary, Secondary · Size: Large, Small · Colour: Normal, Inverse"* and marks it Done. The implemented component exposes `variant: 'primary'|'secondary'` and `size: 'lg'|'sm'` — **no Colour axis.** Worth noting the *states* are fine (hover, active, disabled, focus-visible are all defined for both variants), so "disabled variants" isn't the gap; the Colour axis is. It already has 5 consumers, so adding it later touches all five. 355 2. **Icon Button** — same Inventory spec, also marked Done, **no implementation at all.** 356 357 More broadly: 04.7's status column marks components Done on *design* confirmation, which doesn't imply the implemented API matches. Worth agreeing what "Done" means in that column, since story writers are reading it as readiness. 358 359 --- 360 361 ## Guardrails 362 363 Things to respect while moving fast on all of the above. 364 365 **Tier 1 files.** You hold tier-1-approver / admin, so the verified-session exception applies — you can proceed after naming the file and the reason. Relevant to Play 5's two proposed rules (`.coderabbit/`, `.eslintrc.js`) and to `.github/workflows/`. 366 367 **Four files are absolute** — the exception does *not* apply regardless of approver status: `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. 368 369 **Branches.** Never work on `develop` or `main`. `release/*` is supervised — plan-first, confirm every edit, and code fixes go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch. 370 371 **Squad boundaries.** `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` are shared shell — coordinate with the other squad before touching. `order-summary/` is Tier 2 and Squad B-notified. 372 373 **Commits and PRs** only on explicit request — not as a "natural next step" after finishing work. 374 375 **Scope.** Fixing a bug in a component doesn't license touching the hook it calls. Propose upward refactors; don't do them silently. 376 377 --- 378 379 ## Standing artifacts you own 380 381 | Artifact | Cadence | 382 |---|---| 383 | Refinement checklist (Play 2's challenge list) | Keep current as patterns emerge | 384 | Renderer contract template (Play 4) | Once; sign off per Contentful component | 385 | Per-component accessibility AC set (Play 6) | Once; applied per story | 386 | PR review question list (Play 5) | Review quarterly against what tooling now catches | 387 | Open-items register (Play 8) | Update as items close | 388 | Design-system gap list (Play 9) | Standing design-review agenda | 389 390 --- 391 392 ## First two weeks 393 394 Sequenced by leverage — the first three unblock everything else. 395 396 **Week 1** 397 1. Close the alt-text question with Tim before it propagates into AC 398 2. Get the Contentful pattern decision made (entry-driven vs Studio Experiences per component) — it blocks story order and buildability 399 3. Add the registry line to the BA prompt template — makes Play 1 self-service instead of making you a gate 400 4. Adopt the external-link standard from existing draft AC and close the item 401 402 **Week 2** 403 5. Publish the renderer-contract template and use it on the next Contentful pair 404 6. Communicate the estimation re-baseline once, clearly, in planning 405 7. Take the two Button / Icon Button items to design review 406 8. Raise SFCC-647 so the recommendations question resolves itself 407 9. Put the two enforcement rules up as a decision 408 409 --- 410 411 *Working document. The plays are grounded in what the two sessions actually asked for; the mechanics come from how this repo works today, so both will need updating as the tooling and the backlog move.* 412

You keep the two that need judgement: - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. --- ## Play 2 — Estimation validation *Covers responsibilities 5, 16* Run this before sprint planning, not in it. ### The re-baseline to communicate once M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence: - **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper. - **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.** Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch. If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly. ### Split the two kinds of effort (#16) | Component build | Page composition | |---|---| | Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration | | Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing | | Storybook + tests | Visual validation | | Sized as build work | Sized as validation work | Don't let them be estimated with the same scale. ### Challenge list For each story before it's sized: - [ ] `Origin = Base`? → Copy-first cost is in, or split out - [ ] All variants captured, or only the ones on the first page? - [ ] Accessibility written as AC, or assumed? - [ ] Storybook story accounted for? - [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column) - [ ] Does it depend on anything in Play 8's open list? - [ ] Composition variant hiding as a configuration variant? (Play 3) --- ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review *Covers responsibilities 9, 11* M2's rule: a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. ### The distinction to hold | Kind | Examples | How it's built | |---|---|---| | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. ### Optional-field handling (#11) M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. --- ## Play 4 — The renderer contract *Covers responsibility 10* M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Which pattern a given component uses is still unresolved (Play 8). --- ## Play 5 — PR review *Covers responsibility 4* The useful move here is knowing what the tooling already catches, so your attention goes where it's actually needed. ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time on it | Check | Enforced by | |---|---| | Missing `alt` on `` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | | `onClick` on non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | | Payment credentials logged | semgrep `payment-credential-logged` | | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` | | Type errors, lint, conventional commits | `tsc --noEmit`, lint, commit-msg hook | | Registry freshness | pre-commit hook | ### Not enforced — this is your list | Gap | Why it matters | |---|---| | **Hardcoded hex / px values** in Chakra props and `.scss` | `css.md` states plainly it isn't mechanically enforced. Highest-frequency design-system violation | | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. ### Review questions, in order 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 2. Are all design values tokens? 3. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 4. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 5. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 6. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? --- ## Play 6 — Accessibility *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. ### The per-component AC set (#12) Standing list to apply to every component story: - Keyboard operability and reachability - Focus order and visible focus states - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls - Behaviour when optional content is absent **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate. ### The one open item M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter. **Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision. The BA guide flags it as pending rather than settled. --- ## Play 7 — Page-level validation *Covers responsibilities 13, 15* M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout, design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX. ### Where each part lands today | Ask | Home | |---|---| | Assembled UX / integration | ✅ Playwright E2E — `@area` tags `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations` | | Performance | ✅ `lighthouserc.js` | | Responsive behaviour | ⚠️ Partial — Playwright runs desktop + mobile Chrome, but asserts behaviour, not appearance | | **Spacing / design fidelity / design parity** | ❌ **No automated home.** `testing.md` explicitly excludes visual snapshots from the Vitest budget | **Name this rather than absorbing it.** Design-parity validation is currently manual visual QA. Either it's accepted as manual and the time is resourced, or it's a visual-regression tooling decision (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) — a new dependency and budget, which needs approval before anything is installed. An unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here. Operational note: only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in the change-scoping config. Each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group, or it silently falls back to the full suite. ### Incremental assembly (#15) Tim's build → drop-in → verify loop is well supported and costs nothing to adopt: | Step | Support | |---|---| | Build in isolation | Storybook — mandatory story; `Contentful/` category explicitly allows mock CMS data | | Make available to authors | `npm run generate:contentful` regenerates definitions; pre-commit keeps it in sync | | Author drops it on a page | Studio Experiences — appears once annotated | | Verify | `pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` routes exist | **Caveat worth stating:** this loop only works for Studio Experiences components. Entry-driven ones are wired in code and aren't drag-and-droppable. Another reason the pattern question in Play 8 matters. --- ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing *Covers responsibility 14* These were explicitly left unresolved. Your job is to keep them from being sized on assumption. | Open item | Position to hold | |---|---| | **Alt text** | Confirm with Tim before it lands in AC — Play 6 | | **External links** | Already answered in draft AC (internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Adopt it, bake it into the Link component when built. Doesn't need another meeting | | **Recommendations** | Not actually unknown — `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed, requirement-traced tickets (112, 118, 119, 313, 314, 642, 647, plus 301 under Cart). **SFCC-647 is already `Ready for Development`** and is the one that answers the data-source question. All are Priority `Low`, which is why they surfaced as unknowns. Raise 647; don't create tickets | | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names in circulation for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (M2 + SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7, marked Done), and `shoppableImage` (which already exists in code and delivers exactly the manual curation Bianca described). Resolve to one name per capability before estimating | | **Preview & publishing** | Documented: the preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only, never staging or prod; both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** Settle it now — "can we preview on prod?" is a likely later ask, and it needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale | | **Contentful pattern per component** | Still unresolved after two sessions, and it decides story order, whether the incremental-assembly loop is available, and whether a component is buildable as specified. **Highest-value item to close** | | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across 8 storefronts. Prerequisite to "design variants upfront" | | **Composed-page ownership** | Tim's *"not product/category → Contentful"* rule is a good default but doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks, category landing pages, or promotional tiles in navigation. Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight | **A process note worth acting on.** The Size Selector / Add To Bag split was argued and settled in a Jira comment thread two weeks before M1 re-derived it. Decisions made in refinement need somewhere findable to live, or they get re-litigated. Cheapest fix: when a decision lands, it goes on the story *and* into the relevant Confluence page — not just the thread. --- ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation *Covers responsibility 7* Standing agenda for the design review with Kiera. Two concrete items rather than a general "validate button states": 1. **Button** — 04.7 lists *"Style: Primary, Secondary · Size: Large, Small · Colour: Normal, Inverse"* and marks it Done. The implemented component exposes `variant: 'primary'|'secondary'` and `size: 'lg'|'sm'` — **no Colour axis.** Worth noting the *states* are fine (hover, active, disabled, focus-visible are all defined for both variants), so "disabled variants" isn't the gap; the Colour axis is. It already has 5 consumers, so adding it later touches all five. 2. **Icon Button** — same Inventory spec, also marked Done, **no implementation at all.** More broadly: 04.7's status column marks components Done on *design* confirmation, which doesn't imply the implemented API matches. Worth agreeing what "Done" means in that column, since story writers are reading it as readiness. --- ## Guardrails Things to respect while moving fast on all of the above. **Tier 1 files.** You hold tier-1-approver / admin, so the verified-session exception applies — you can proceed after naming the file and the reason. Relevant to Play 5's two proposed rules (`.coderabbit/`, `.eslintrc.js`) and to `.github/workflows/`. **Four files are absolute** — the exception does *not* apply regardless of approver status: `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. **Branches.** Never work on `develop` or `main`. `release/*` is supervised — plan-first, confirm every edit, and code fixes go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch. **Squad boundaries.** `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` are shared shell — coordinate with the other squad before touching. `order-summary/` is Tier 2 and Squad B-notified. **Commits and PRs** only on explicit request — not as a "natural next step" after finishing work. **Scope.** Fixing a bug in a component doesn't license touching the hook it calls. Propose upward refactors; don't do them silently. --- ## Standing artifacts you own | Artifact | Cadence | |---|---| | Refinement checklist (Play 2's challenge list) | Keep current as patterns emerge | | Renderer contract template (Play 4) | Once; sign off per Contentful component | | Per-component accessibility AC set (Play 6) | Once; applied per story | | PR review question list (Play 5) | Review quarterly against what tooling now catches | | Open-items register (Play 8) | Update as items close | | Design-system gap list (Play 9) | Standing design-review agenda | --- ## First two weeks Sequenced by leverage — the first three unblock everything else. **Week 1** 1. Close the alt-text question with Tim before it propagates into AC 2. Get the Contentful pattern decision made (entry-driven vs Studio Experiences per component) — it blocks story order and buildability 3. Add the registry line to the BA prompt template — makes Play 1 self-service instead of making you a gate 4. Adopt the external-link standard from existing draft AC and close the item **Week 2** 5. Publish the renderer-contract template and use it on the next Contentful pair 6. Communicate the estimation re-baseline once, clearly, in planning 7. Take the two Button / Icon Button items to design review 8. Raise SFCC-647 so the recommendations question resolves itself 9. Put the two enforcement rules up as a decision --- *Working document. The plays are grounded in what the two sessions actually asked for; the mechanics come from how this repo works today, so both will need updating as the tooling and the backlog move.*

content.thinking: I'm going to re-evaluate those 10 stories through my FED Lead Playbook framework, which structures how I approach technical decisions. The first play focuses on the reuse hierarchy—checking whether we can leverage existing Salesforce or PWA Kit capabilities before building new shared components. The playbook includes a component registry and worked examples that are already verified: the size selector uses the base `swatch-group/`, add-to-bag extends `product-view/index.jsx` which already handles cart calls and bundle logic, max purchase quantity uses `quantity-picker/`, and variant resolution relies on existing hooks like `use-controlled-variations` and `use-derived-product`. Importantly, the playbook explicitly flags that SFCC-650's description mentions "Cart API integration in scope," but since the base product-view already performs the cart call, that story should be reframed as extending product-view rather than building new cart integration—which means my earlier 5-point estimate was off base. The first story against any given base component bears the copy-first cost, and since multiple stories in this batch touch the same base components, I need to identify who pays that tax. Component estimates should go up while page estimates go down when I split component build from page composition. For SFCC-723 and the pdp/hero gallery carousel, the 2x2 grid layout is a composition variant, not a config variant—`showGalleryButton` is config, but the grid structure itself belongs in a container/slot component, which validates my instinct to split the gallery out. The PR review play catches that the ast-grep rule only matches lowercase `` tags, so Chakra's `` component isn't covered, and hardcoded hex values and pixel units aren't being enforced either—relevant to badges, swatches, and recently-viewed components that use images. Accessibility needs to move from WCAG 2.1 to 2.2 AA baseline per SFCC-648, with alt text as an open item and five accessibility criteria per component. Page-level validation has no automated home for design parity, and the E2E `@area` tags only map `e2e_homepage` for change-scoping, so the pdp specs need a new allow-list group. Before sizing, I should register open items—notably that SFCC-647 (Recommendations) is already Ready for Development and directly answers the data-source question I raised for SFCC-84 and SFCC-83 on Recently Viewed. There's also the "Shop the Look" naming question with four options. The design system escalation reveals that Button lacks a Colour axis—the spec calls for Primary/Secondary plus Large/Small plus Normal/Inverse, but the implementation only has variant and size, missing the colour dimension entirely. Now I'm seeing that Icon Button has zero implementation at all, which is a critical blocker. The `pdp/add-to-bag` component (SFCC-650) expects to use the base Button with Primary and Large, which maps to variant='primary' and size='lg'—that works. But if the design calls for Inverse colour, there's a gap. And SFCC-434 for Add to Wishlist is an icon button, so the missing Icon Button implementation is a hard prerequisite I didn't flag before. I need to verify these codebase claims rather than relying on the playbook. Let me check the key dependencies in parallel: whether `.claude/registry/components.md` exists, if the base `product-view` handles addToCart, if `quantity-picker` is implemented, confirm the Button component's variant/size axes without colour, verify Icon Button's status, check the Chakra `` versus `` ast-grep rule, and review the e2e change-scoping allow-list groups. This is a read-only analysis on the release/v0.1.0 branch, so I can run these checks efficiently.…

The registry is a couple weeks out of date, but the pre-commit hook keeps it fresh whenever the app components change. I'm verifying that the Button component is custom-built with five consumers, supporting primary and secondary variants plus large and small sizes, and importantly, it has no color axis—which aligns with what I found in Play 9.

Now I'm scanning through the other components: SwatchGroup and ProductView are base tier components with no active consumers, QuantityPicker exists as a base, and ProductTile is interesting because it already has a `badgeDetails` prop for array-based badges, which directly supports the SFCC-132 badge work. ProductScroller is the recently viewed rail component with native scroll snapping and manual controls. I'm also noting that product-view has `maxOrderQuantity` as a prop with validation logic and cart management hooks, which is exactly what SFCC-196 needs for max purchase quantity enforcement—the base already has this capability built in.

I need to verify…

content.text:
Playbook read and its codebase claims verified against the repo. Every Play-1/5/7/9 assertion holds, and the registry surfaced **more reuse than the playbook lists** — which materially changes four of the ten estimates. Registry caveat: last regenerated 2026-07-31, but no `overrides/app/**` changes since, so it's effectively current.

---

# What changes vs. my first pass

| Story | First pass | Playbook-driven revision |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC-650 add-to-bag | "5 — real cart mutation" | **Reframe as *extend `product-view`*.** Base already does the cart call, modal, toast → **3** |
| SFCC-91 / 708 colour | "AC contradicts itself; needs a decision" | **Base already does both modes** — `as={href ? RouteLink : 'button'}`. The "full page reload" AC is wrong *against the base*, not just against PRD-062 |
| SFCC-196 max qty | "base capability, ~3–5" | Base `maxOrderQuantity` only feeds QuantityPicker's `max`. **Zimmermann has no qty picker → base doesn't cover it** → **5** |
| SFCC-84/83 Recently Viewed | "storage backend unknown" | Not unknown — **Play 8: SFCC-647 is already `Ready for Development`** and answers it. Raise 647, don't spike |
| SFCC-434 wishlist | "5" | `useWishList` exists, **but IconButton has no implementation at all** → hard design-system prerequisite |
| SFCC-723 hero | "split the gallery, probably" | **Play 3 doctrine: the 2×2 grid is a *composition* variant** → container component, not a prop. Split is required, not preferred |

---

# Play 1 — Reuse & dependency ladder (all ten)

Verified against `.claude/registry/components.md` + the base package.

| Story | What already exists | Origin · Tier | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **650** add-to-bag | `product-view/index.jsx` — `addToCart`, `updateCart`, `useAddToCartModalContext`, `showToast`, `validateOrderability`; `Button` (Custom, 5 consumers) | Base · T4 | **Extend base.** AC says "cart API integration in scope" — it isn't, it's already there |
| **648** size-selector | `swatch-group/` — `role="radiogroup"`, `role="radio"`, `aria-checked`, square/circle variants, existing test | Base · **T2** | ⚠️ **Fit is questionable** — see below |
| **723** hero | `image-gallery/` (no 2×2, no video controls) | Base · **T2** | New composition; gallery = separate |
| **91/708** colour swatches | `swatch-group/swatch.jsx` — `as={href ? RouteLink : 'button'}`, `to={href}`, `aria-label={name}` | Base · **T2** | **Extend base — it already covers both models** |
| **196** max qty | `maxOrderQuantity` prop → QuantityPicker `max` only | Base · T4 | **Doesn't fit** — justify new build |
| **434** wishlist | `useWishList` hook; `ProductTile` `enableFavourite/isFavourite/onFavouriteToggle` | Base · T4 · **Squad B** | Extend hook; **IconButton missing** |
| **132** badges | `ProductTile` already has **`badgeDetails?: array`** | Base · **T2** | Existing badge shape — align with SFCC-236 |
| **84** see-full-history | `ProductScroller` (scroll-snap + manual controls) for the rail; shared card via SFCC-236 | Base · T4 | Extend base |
| **25** variation model | Enables `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product` | — | BM config; no FE reuse angle |
| **268** max-qty config | — | — | BM config |

### ⚠️ The reuse question worth the most in the room — SFCC-648

Base `swatch-group` is a **radiogroup of swatches**. But SFCC-648's ACs 1–3 describe *"default state with placeholder label" → "filled state" → "focus/open showing all size options"* plus a distinct **mobile variant**. That's a **dropdown/listbox**, not a swatch row — and the base has no size dropdown.

**Ask:** is the size selector a swatch row (extend `swatch-group`, cheap) or a dropdown (new build, and AC#14's arrow-key model becomes listbox semantics, not radio)? This single answer moves the estimate from 3 to 8.

### The copy-first tax — name it once, pay it once

Every base component above is **not yet in `overrides/`**, so AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (copy → TS → `tsc` → console.log marker → **human confirms** → build) applies to whoever touches it first. Six components are implicated across this batch:

`product-view` · `swatch-group` (T2) · `image-gallery` (T2) · `breadcrumb` (T2) · `display-price` (T2) · `product-scroller`

**Recommendation:** one **PDP scaffold enabler story** that pays copy-first for all six in a single human-gated pass. Otherwise the tax lands unpredictably on whichever story is picked up first and that story blows its estimate — precisely Jasmijn's recurring concern.

---

# Play 3 — Configuration vs composition variant

| Story | Variant | Kind | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 723 | `showGalleryButton` | **Configuration** | Prop on one component ✅ |
| 723 | single full-width ↔ **4-up 2×2 grid** ↔ video item ↔ dot indicator | **Composition** | **Container/slot component** — structurally a second component |

So `pdp/hero` as written is really **two** stories: the hero layout (3) and a gallery/carousel container (~8). Pricing the grid as a prop under-estimates it. Same logic applies to the expanded-gallery view that SFCC-708's rollover swatches live in — a third surface.

---

# Play 2 — Revised estimates (component build vs page composition split)

| Story | Component build | Page composition | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **648** size-selector | **5** (swatch row) / **8** (dropdown) | — | Blocked on the fit question |
| **650** add-to-bag | **3** | — | Extend `product-view`; +2 if it pays copy-first |
| **723** hero | **3** | — | Hero only |
| *(new)* gallery/carousel | **8** | — | Split out of 723 |
| **91** colour swatches | **5** | — | Both swatch modes + rollover preview |
| **196** max qty | **5** | — | Basket-count logic, no base fit |
| **434** wishlist | **5** | — | + IconButton prerequisite |
| **132** badges | **3–5** | — | Reuses `badgeDetails` |
| **84** see-full-history | — | **3** | Page assembly over shared card |
| **25** variation model | **3–5** (config) | — | BM |
| **268** max-qty config | **2** (config) | — | BM |
| *(new)* PDP scaffold enabler | **3–5** | — | Copy-first for 6 base components |

**The re-baseline to say out loud once:** component numbers here are *higher* than the old page-level equivalents (all-variants-upfront + a11y AC + mandatory Storybook + copy-first), and page numbers are *lower*. If only the second half lands, the programme will look faster than it is.

---

# Play 4 — Renderer contract

**Not applicable to this batch.** None of the ten are Contentful-backed — all SFCC product data. Worth stating explicitly so the contract template isn't demanded here; it applies to the footer pair (SFCC-117) and editorial modules instead.

---

# Play 5 — PR review gaps that bite this batch specifically

| Gap | Why it hits these ten |
|---|---|
| **`img-missing-alt` has `regex: ^img$`** — lowercase only | Base `<Image>` has **10 consumers**. Swatches, badges, recently-viewed tiles and the gallery are *all* `<Image>`-based → **alt review is manual on every story here** |
| **Hardcoded hex / px** unenforced | This is a design-system-heavy batch straight from Figma — highest-risk moment for token violations |
| **Duplication / reuse** unenforced | Badge rendering could easily be built twice (SFCC-132 PDP vs SFCC-236 card). Human check only |
| **Complexity / size** unenforced | `pdp/hero` composing 6+ children is the likely offender |

---

# Play 6 — Accessibility

| Item | Action |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ **WCAG version** | SFCC-648, 650, 723 all commit to **2.1 AA**. Project baseline is **2.2 AA** → correct all three and fix the story template so it stops propagating |
| **650 `disabled` vs `aria-disabled`** | AC#1 (`disabled`) conflicts with AC#2 (click shows "Size required") and AC#10 (announced as unavailable). A native `disabled` button can't be clicked or focused → use `aria-disabled` |
| **648 semantics** | If it's a dropdown, `role="radio"` (base) is wrong — needs listbox/combobox semantics. Ties to the fit question |
| **91/708 swatches** | Base already gives `aria-label={name}` + `aria-checked` ✅. But `role="radio"` on an `href` swatch that *navigates* is semantically odd — decide radio vs link for the cross-product case |
| **434 wishlist icon** | Icon-only control → `aria-label` + pressed state announced (ast-grep catches the label, not the state) |
| **Alt-text open item** | Still unconfirmed with Tim. Affects every image-bearing story here — get it closed before it lands in ten sets of AC |

---

# Play 7 — Page-level validation

| Finding | Action |
|---|---|
| **No `e2e_pdp` allow-list group in `qa.yml`** — only `e2e_homepage` exists | The first PDP spec silently falls back to the **full suite** on every develop PR. Add the group with the first PDP spec |
| **Design parity has no automated home** | This batch is almost entirely visual/design-fidelity work. Either resource manual visual QA or raise visual-regression tooling as a budget decision — don't absorb it |
| Story tags | Every new spec needs `@pdp` **and** `@SFCC-NNN` for change-scoping + BrowserStack/Zephyr |

---

# Play 8 — Hold these before sizing

| Open item | Bearing on this batch |
|---|---|
| **SFCC-647 (`Ready for Development`)** | Answers the Recently Viewed data-source question → **unblocks SFCC-83/84 without a spike.** Raise it, don't create tickets |
| **Alt text** | Ten image-bearing stories waiting on one decision |
| **`regions` model** | SFCC-132 AC#6 gates badges by region (AU-only). Region mechanism unconfirmed → prerequisite to "all variants upfront" |
| **Shop the Look naming** (4 names, incl. existing `shoppableImage` in code) | PDP hosts it — resolve before any PDP editorial story is sized |
| **Composed-page ownership** | PDP editorial blocks (Shop the Look, Seen on the Runway) unsettled — affects hero's slot contract |
| **Accessories with colour but no size** (SFCC-25, Dani) | Decides `pdp/size-selector`'s one-size path |
| **Wishlist one-size-per-product (CRM-127/128) vs per-colour (AC#6)** | Unreconciled; changes 434's logic |

**Process note, live in this batch:** the Size Selector / Add-to-Bag split was settled in a Jira thread, re-derived in M1, and now exists as *both* SFCC-92 and SFCC-648/650 (+ duplicates 293/295). That's the exact failure mode Play 8 warns about. **Retire/reframe SFCC-92 and record the decision in Confluence, not just the thread.**

---

# Play 9 — Design-system escalation (now a blocker, not an agenda item)

| Gap | Impact here |
|---|---|
| **IconButton — spec marked Done in 04.7, zero implementation.** No registry row; only Chakra's `IconButton` used inline in `header/index.tsx` | **Blocks SFCC-434** (wishlist icon). Also needed for gallery video controls (723) and carousel arrows |
| **Button — no Colour axis.** 04.7 specifies Normal/Inverse; implemented exposes `variant` + `size` only. **5 consumers already** | SFCC-650 needs Primary/Large — fine today. But if any PDP CTA needs Inverse, this touches all five consumers |

Both go to the Kiera review this week, and IconButton should be logged as a prerequisite story ahead of SFCC-434.

---

# Guardrails triggered

| Guardrail | Flag |
|---|---|
| **Tier 2 — non-author PR review + Squad B coordination** | `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `product-tile`, `display-price`, `breadcrumb` — five of six copy-first targets |
| **Tier 1 — consume, never modify** | `use-current-basket` (SFCC-196, 650 both read basket state) |
| **Cross-squad** | `useWishList` is registry-assigned **Squad B**; SFCC-434 is labelled Squad-A → coordinate |
| **Branch** | We're on `release/v0.1.0` (supervised). None of this work lands here — feature branches off `develop` |

---

## The six actions I'd take out of the room

1. **Answer the SFCC-648 fit question** (swatch row vs dropdown) — biggest single estimate swing in the batch.
2. **Create the PDP scaffold enabler story** so copy-first is paid once, visibly, rather than ambushing whichever story goes first.
3. **Split the gallery/carousel out of SFCC-723** on Play 3 grounds (composition ≠ configuration).
4. **Reframe SFCC-650 as "extend `product-view`"** and correct the "cart API integration in scope" line.
5. **Fix SFCC-708/91's "full page reload" AC** — base `swatch.jsx` already does client-side `RouteLink`, and PRD-062 requires no reload.
6. **Log IconButton as a prerequisite** and raise SFCC-647 — two cheap moves that unblock 434 and 83/84 respectively.

Two template fixes to land alongside: **WCAG 2.2** as the story-template default, and the `aria-disabled` pattern for any "disabled until valid" CTA.

Want me to draft the enabler story and the gallery/carousel story, or write the AC corrections as Jira comments for your review before posting? Also worth noting the Figma connector is still unauthenticated in this session — I can't read the Design System 2026 frames the three draft stories cite, so all design-parity claims here come from the tickets and `.docs/`, not the source of truth.
